The picks

Chosen for the recipient and use described, using published product information. We have not hands-on tested these products.

  1. 1. Students whose instructor recommends this format

    ASA pilot logbook

    A useful first purchase only if the school recommends this format and the student does not already have it.

    An affordable way to mark the start of flight training. Pair it with a note about the journey ahead, rather than filling in any flight-record pages yourself.

    Keep in mind
    Another logbook can be redundant if they have a preferred paper book or digital system.
    Before you choose
    Check with their instructor first: they may already have a logbook or use a different format.
    $9.49Listed 2026-10-20View at Pilot Mall↗
  2. 2. Students learning paper navigation

    ASA CP-1 Fixed Plotter

    Appropriate for a student learning paper cross-country planning; ask whether it is already in the school kit.

    A small, inexpensive tool with chart scales and a course protractor.

    Keep in mind
    Duplicates a tool many school starter kits already contain.
    Before you choose
    Match the chart scale and the instructor’s equipment list.
    $10.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  3. 3. Pilots who take paper notes

    SKILCRAFT B3 Aviator pen

    Black ink, red ink and a pencil in one everyday tool. An uncomplicated addition to a practical gift bundle, especially with a handwritten note.

    Keep in mind
    Its utility is limited for someone who keeps all notes digitally.
    Before you choose
    Check whether they prefer paper notes; an all-digital pilot may get less use from it.
    $24.50Listed 2026-10-20View at Pilot Mall↗
  4. 4. Students whose instructor recommends this book

    The Student Pilot’s Flight Manual, 12th edition

    Buy the instructor-approved edition, not a second syllabus selected on the student’s behalf.

    A structured print manual is useful when it matches the school’s approach.

    Keep in mind
    Unrequested textbooks can duplicate or conflict with an existing course.
    Before you choose
    Confirm the twelfth edition with the instructor before purchasing.
    $44.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  5. 5. Pilots looking for a compact backpack-style flight bag

    Flight Gear Stealth Bag

    A flight bag is a gift they can use beyond the holidays. This compact backpack-style option is worth a look when their current setup is an overflowing ordinary bag.

    Keep in mind
    A compact flight bag may be too small for a pilot who carries a full day’s equipment.
    Before you choose
    Compare the listed dimensions with their headset, tablet and usual load before choosing.
    $79.95Listed 2026-10-20View at Sporty’s↗
  6. 6. Pilots using a compatible tablet and case

    Flight Gear rotating kneeboard

    A practical way to keep a compatible iPad in reach. It is most useful when you already know the pilot wants a kneeboard rather than a mounted tablet.

    Keep in mind
    The wrong tablet or cockpit fit can make an otherwise useful accessory awkward to use.
    Before you choose
    Confirm the exact iPad model, case and preferred cockpit setup with the retailer.
    $22.95Listed 2026-10-20View at Sporty’s↗
  7. 7. Pilots who requested a compact red/white light

    Flight Gear Aviator’s Light

    A compact light with separate red and white controls. It makes sense for the person who likes keeping small, useful tools in their flight bag.

    Keep in mind
    Easy to duplicate if their existing flight bag is already well equipped.
    Before you choose
    Ask what light they already carry; this is an accessory, not a replacement for required equipment.

  9. 9. Pilots with a personal connection to the Cessna 172

    Cessna 172 Skyhawk model

    The best model is often the aircraft with a story behind it. This mahogany Skyhawk is especially thoughtful for someone who learned to fly a Cessna 172.

    A finished display model offers no building activity; choose a kit if assembling it is part of the appeal.

Start with the instructor’s list

Before buying training equipment, find out what the school already supplies and what the instructor expects the student to bring. A duplicate logbook or an incompatible tablet holder is less helpful than a simple gift card. You do not need to understand every piece of equipment: ask the student for a photo or link to their list. If you want to keep the surprise, ask which category is still missing without choosing a model yet.

For the first few lessons

A modest, practical gift is often enough. A logbook can mark the beginning of training if the school has not already supplied one. A pen is easy to add, and a compact light may be useful as the student builds a flight bag. Keep a gift receipt. Avoid buying a complete bundle simply because it says student pilot; the school may have a different syllabus, preferred materials or equipment requirements.

For someone already training

Pay attention to what they carry. A compact flight bag can help if everything currently goes into a general backpack. A kneeboard makes sense only if it fits their exact tablet and they prefer that setup in the cockpit. Ask about the tablet case as well as the iPad model. A headset is a bigger decision: make it a choose-together gift with the student and instructor instead of guessing at connectors or fit.

Make a milestone gift personal

For a first solo or certificate, the story can matter more than the price. A model of the aircraft they actually flew is a better match than a more expensive model of an unrelated airplane. Confirm the type and variant before buying. Add a handwritten note with the date and the moment you are celebrating. For a flight lesson contribution, arrange payment directly with the school and confirm how credit is applied and whether it expires.

What should you avoid?

Do not assume that a flight simulator accessory, training course or navigation subscription matches their instructor’s plan. Ask first. A gift should support training without creating a second system the student has to learn. If you cannot verify compatibility, choose a keepsake or a retailer gift card and let them select their own equipment.

Prices and availability can change. Check the exact model, delivered total and return terms with the seller. Our recommendations are researched editorial selections, not hands-on test results.
